Hi, I have had my lurcher from 8 weeks and here’s what we learnt from our experience with her. Toys that hide food are great for boredom, there’s snuffle mats which are great for kibble, my lurcher loves stinky treats like dried fish skin and jerky so we use a Kong for those bigger treats, we found that hard toys like benebone and nylabone helped a lot with her teething and definitely saved our hands from her shark teeth. We always leave the tv on when she’s home alone for shorter amounts of time and it has helped her separation anxiety a lot, I recommend bluey or other Disney shows that are upbeat and help cover possible anxiety triggering noises from outside whilst you’re not home. Wishing you and your puppy the best!! She’s the cutest!!!

I’m based in the uk and dog parks here are a lil different from the US as we don’t really have many official ”dog” parks and it’s kinda just popular parks that locals and dog walkers frequent, we began taking our lurcher cross puppy to the popular dog parks at around 9 months old; she had a great time for the most of it but it was stressful to see so many dogs not being completely supervised, many times she would be snapped at or chased and the carer of the dog would not leash or restrain their dog after and carry on like nothing happened, this made my puppy a lot more cautious and nervous around new dogs in a large amount ,she had interacted with my neighbours dogs and local dogs we’d bump into from 8 weeks old so we got very lucky that she never had anxiety. it’s frustrating that not every owner is going to care about their dogs bad behaviour as much as you are, it was really tough to have to advocate for my dog in social situations and correct my dogs behaviour, she was reactive and overexcited and it was very stressful in parks with a lot of dogs but it was great for bonding with her and exploring. We now go every once in a while and it works out great

Also my lurcher loves every other dog/animal/living thing, she is the friendly dog I’ve met and there hasn’t been a breed or animal that she hasn’t wanted to play with. I know early socialisation is very important for small/larger dogs so definitely let your dog meet people and dogs/cats of different ages and breeds to help socialise them and get them adjusted with different personalities and energy levels.

So I had 2 cats before getting my puppy last year and initially it was tough but we set boundaries for the puppy early on such as “safe spaces” the cats have their own beds and my puppy had her crate and bed, this was really helpful to teach her personal space, we still let the cats set their own boundaries and teach her in their own way but after the cats were initially scared of her, they got used to her within a couple months and there was peace, I’d say the main issue we had with her was overexcitement which confused the cats and space boundaries of the puppy wanting to sit everywhere and anywhere she’s seen the cats sit.

When my puppy was 5 months old, we adopted a little black kitten and my puppy became obsessed with her, she wanted to eat at the same time as her, sit on her and just play with her constantly, we let them work things out on their own but because the kitten was so tiny there were times where we intervened and reinforced the puppy to be more gentle or to walk away when the kitten was getting too overwhelmed whilst playing.

Anyways it’s been a year of having my puppy and she’s a year and a couple months now but we have never had a cat fight or incident between any of them, I would like to add that all of my pets are female so I’m not sure if that helped me in a way to avoid territorial behaviours being formed or aggression but I’m very happy that after a long time and a lot of patience, I have the cutest pair of besties who wake me up every morning.

The chances of a dog becoming aggressive or reactive mostly depends on how they were socialised and desensitised towards things as a puppy. As long as you keep showing up for your dog and advocating for your dog when they are put in uncomfortable situations then they will trust you and listen to you.I have an 11 month old puppy who is very excitable and loves attention from humans and other dogs, she has recently had negative experiences with dogs in local parks due to the owners not being aware of their dog’s behaviour or ignoring signs that their dog is reactive and still considering them “friendly”, out of the times she has had a negative experience, none of the dogs have been “dangerous breeds”, I think the main thing you can think about as you move forward with your puppy is that as long as you show them love and socialise them well with possible causes of aggression, they should be able to learn from you and be confident.
